scope: Cases 1 and 3 only; case 2 retained from runs/20261023-102333 because its relevant guidance did not change.
grading: Manual semantic review against unchanged evals-frozen.json. Per-cell grading.json contains quoted evidence. Raw practice-oriented grader scores remain in results.json and harness-benchmark.json and are not reporting-quality results.
isolation: The harness self-test passed including planted contaminants before execution. Cells ran outside git with ambient instruction files and auto-memory disabled, settings restricted to project/local, no phase prompts, and paired arms interleaved.
comparison: Tightened current method-based-report/shared foundations versus no skill using Claude CLI. This is not a Codex-versus-Claude benchmark or an isolated experiment on the two added sentences.

metric_definitions.mean_pass_rate: Mean of one frozen discriminating check per case; checks were selected after the first run, before this rerun. Not a general report-quality rate.
metric_definitions.tokens: CLI input_tokens + output_tokens; excludes cache creation/read tokens and is not total context consumption

changes_observed: With-skill programme report now explicitly treats contracting/invoicing as unknown and labels interim billing as proposed, repairing the prior invention.
With-skill programme report explicitly distinguishes credentials from staffing, support processes and commercial appetite.
The broader frozen commercial diagnostic still fails because participant economics are incompletely tested; training-readiness and delivery-capacity gating remain incomplete.

Both comparison reports still invent unified internal fault ownership. The with-skill internal-credential caveat passes the narrow frozen assertion but is less explicit about applicability than its first-run counterpart.
The no-skill programme rerun independently added proposed owners, unlike its first output. It still lacks explicit success evidence for each priority. This illustrates run-to-run variability.

comparison_to_first_iteration.frozen_scored_checks: Same result for rerun cases: with-skill 2/2, without-skill 0/2. No improvement in the aggregate frozen checks from the added sentences.
comparison_to_first_iteration.shared_gap_diagnostics: Still 3 shared failing diagnostics across the two cases. Specific contracting and credential wording improved inside those broad diagnostics, so the repair is partial.

limitations: No general uplift claim: two repeated synthetic cases and single outputs per arm cannot establish reliable general performance.
Frozen checks originated from post-hoc review of the first outputs; these cases are not a fresh holdout.
Whole skill/foundation context differs between arms, and model variability is visible in the baseline. The rerun does not establish causality for individual sentences.
The existing harness omits full CLI transcripts, model identifier and cache-token metrics; no missing numbers have been invented.
Do not call the practice-oriented --rescore for these reports: it will overwrite this manually reviewed semantic benchmark.
